column1: # Math typed in a table cell: the same shortcuts as in the page, then the cell's own keys.
# The note is a 2×3 table; keys go to its first body cell (c1), set from `before`.
# before<TAB>keys<TAB>expected cell[<TAB>stored row]. `@r,c:` in front: the keys moved to that cell
# (Tab selects the next cell's text). `exited`: they left the table. Stored rows have spaces squeezed.
# Keys: ⇥ Tab, ⇤ Shift-Tab, ⏎ Return, ⌫ Backspace, ⎋ Escape, ↶ Undo, ↷ Redo.
# Auto-fraction, as in the page (and after a subscript: chemical formulas).
# Tab through the blanks and out of the equation; only then to the next cell.
# Outside math, Tab and Shift-Tab move between cells and Return goes down a row.
# Return leaves the cell even mid-shortcut (keeping what's written); Escape leaves the table.
# Undo after an expansion brings back what was typed; Redo the expansion.
# A price is not an equation, and an escaped dollar opens nothing.
# A bare | would split the row: shortcuts that write bars use commands in a cell.
# A bar typed by hand is kept, and escaped in the file; the rendered table currently reads that `\|` as ‖.
# One line only: display-math shortcuts that need lines of their own stay as typed.
